title: Detect duplicate TensorView claims after canonical sort
finding: TensorView already canonically sorts every retained sparse entry, but construction also maintained a separate Python set containing every (coordinates, relation) semantic key solely to reject duplicates. At the declared one-million-entry ceiling that duplicates O(n) semantic-key retention during construction even though identical semantic claims are necessarily adjacent after the mandatory canonical sort.
primary_claim: TensorView now reuses its mandatory canonical ordering as the duplicate-detection boundary: after sorting, adjacent entries are compared by coordinates and relation and duplicate claims still fail closed. The extra full semantic-key hash set is removed. Fourfold/Forest authority, revision/provenance identity, tensor status, canonical ordering and wire contracts remain unchanged.
gardener_decision: Reuse the mandatory canonical sort for duplicate detection rather than retaining a second full semantic-key index. Do not add a cache, index service, alternate TensorView type, planner, store, registry, scheduler or sparse backend for an invariant the existing ordering already exposes.
acceptance: TensorView construction does not retain and hash one extra semantic-key record per sparse entry solely for duplicate detection
canonical TensorView entry ordering remains deterministic
duplicate coordinate/relation claims still fail closed even when masked/value/evidence fields differ
adversarial prevalidated relation values that refuse hashing do not break construction of unique claims
the affected Fourfold/Tensor contract matrix and isolated wheel execute successfully on the exact code/test revision
repository-wide CI evidence remains collection-only rather than a full-suite execution claim
no OwnerApproval, promotion, gate transition, measured memory/latency improvement or benchmark superiority claim is created
